Laura Chen: Quick sync after the allocator RFC: proposing a lightweight bounded compaction runner + retire window to avoid late-write DMA stomps. Sketch below.
Evan Brooks: Short question how do we avoid compacting hot pages and causing thrash?
Laura Chen: Two things: 1) 1% sampled EMA hotness per page; runner skips pages above hot_threshold. 2) per-tenant defrag_aggressiveness flag.
Maya Lin: Sampling seems fine, but how do we keep reader perf stable with indirection?
Laura Chen: Keep header tiny: (ptr, seq). Reader does atomic read of both before/after access, retry only on seq change or odd seq. Common case is a single atomic read.
Rohan Singh: Retire semantics? important for late DMA completions.
Laura Chen: On migrate, mark old page RETIRING with retire_epoch=current_epoch+hold. Default hold=1 epoch. Runner only returns retired pages after epoch expires.
Evan Brooks: Cost model for cross-pool moves? we must avoid PCIe thrash.
Laura Chen: Linear estimator: cost_move = bytes/est_bw + pcie_latency + cpu_cost. Benefit = sample_faults * avg_fault_cost. Move if benefit*profit_factor > cost_move. Calibrate via telemetry.
Maya Lin: What about atomic races when runner frees and allocator reuses? retire-list solves most, but need forced_reclaim path under memory pressure.
Laura Chen: Yes: add forced_reclaim which zeros and fences page before reuse; increment reclaimed_under_pressure_count. Also expose max_retired_ratio to avoid resident blowup.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: will canary branch "epochal-defrag-v2" on lab-cluster-5 :eyes:
Rohan Singh: Rollout plan: prototype + unit tests, lab canary with epoch_ms=50 pages_limit=128, then perf on embeddings. Watch header_retry_rate, retired_ratio, p95 token latency.
Laura Chen: Thanks. I'll open a WIP PR with prototype and perf harness. Volunteers to review?
Maya Lin: I'll do sampling + metrics.
Evan Brooks: I'll review atomic header and retire logic.
Laura Chen: Awesome  will post short design note and diagrams in the RFC PR. :thumbsup:
